# Peer-key discovery vectors, version 3

`cases.json` is generated by the production `peer_keys_response` in
`crates/fed-module/src/main.rs`; the `fed_not_ready` refusal comes from its
production handler. `callosum.peer_keys_read` is local-only and accepts any
local caller. Params are ignored. Caller authority comes from the daemon,
never request JSON.

Version 3 retains every version 2 case and adds the NATS bus seal public key,
`bus_seal_x25519`. Only the `reserved:ckbus`, `reserved:claustrum` and
`reserved:engram` callers see that kind. These identities are set by the
local daemon from the module's verified launch, never claimed by the caller. Engram seals agent-move keys to
the same public key; the vault keeps the uses apart by requiring a
per-caller HPKE `info` prefix when it opens. `vault_transfer_x25519` and
`fleet_epoch_wrap_x25519` remain claustrum-only, as do `class` and
`pairing_id`. Classes are `computer`, `phone`, `sim` or `unknown`; pairing ids
are the opaque `<incarnation>:<ceremony counter>` returned by
`paired_devices_read`. The class, pairing id and keys are read in one store
snapshot. All other key kinds remain visible to every local caller.
If filtering leaves no kinds, the reply omits `key_record` instead of
returning an empty map.

The bus cases show claustrum's full view, ckbus's bus and verification keys,
and an ordinary caller's verification keys with the bus and vault-only kinds
removed. A bus-only record is omitted for an ordinary caller. The two engram
cases (tag `peer-keys-vectors-v3.1`) show engram's view, which matches ckbus's.
They are appended after the v3.0 cases, which stay byte-identical. Every
version 2 reply remains byte-identical. `peers` outside `reply` describes the input
fixture; null optional input fields are omitted in replies.

Each kind's `pub` is lowercase hex bounded by fed-wire §6 only; consumers
check lengths themselves. The intentionally short fixture keys demonstrate
that the wire shape does not promise a cryptographic key length. Each kind's
`version` is its own vault generation as a decimal string, not a JSON number
or shared record version. The bus seal key is read from `kem:bus-seal:1`.

Regenerate from the repository root (on the Linux build server):

```sh
UPDATE_PEER_KEYS_VECTORS=1 cargo test --locked -p fed-module --bin ck-callosum peer_keys_vectors_tests::vectors_match_production -- --exact --nocapture
```

Run without the environment variable to check drift. After regeneration,
update `SHA256SUMS` and the pins in `test-vectors/scan-vendored-ids.py`.
The published `test-vectors/peer-keys/` and `test-vectors/peer-keys-v2/` files
must not be changed.
